topic: Insurance free-look period: 30 days from receiving the policy document for new life and individual health policies; refund minus proportionate risk premium, medical-exam cost and stamp duty, within 7 days (illustrative ₹50,000 premium)
experiment: EXPLOIT (contrarian-number: 'the premium isn't gone, you have 30 days'). Applies the 24 Oct co-buyer send rule to insurance: send target is the friend who just bought a policy (festive-season and bank-counter buys). 5 scenes, 33 vo words, ~14 s.
caption:
Regret a policy you just bought? Did you know you have 30 days?

Insurance rules give new life and individual health policies a 30-day free-look period, counted from the day you receive the policy document.
Cancel inside it and you get the premium back, minus only cover for the days used, any medical-test cost and stamp duty.
The refund is due within 7 days of your request. (ULIPs refund at the day's unit value. Renewals, portability and policies under a year are excluded.)
Illustrative: on a ₹50,000 premium, that's most of the money back.
